articles.title: 'This would definitely help': How Bellingham's underwear billboard ad in New York reflects football's growing US appeal
articles.summary: Jude Bellingham has added another milestone to his growing list of achievements, this time away from the football pitch.
articles.body: Jude Bellingham has added another milestone to his growing list of achievements, this time away from the football pitch. The England and Real Madrid midfielder features on a giant Calvin Klein underwear billboard in Manhattan, New York, joining a list of celebrities who have appeared on the fashion brand's famous SoHo billboard.Measuring 75 feet by 55 feet (22.9 by 16.8 metres), the billboard overlooks one of New York's busiest shopping areas and has drawn crowds of people stopping to take photographs. Bellingham is seen striking his trademark arms-stretched celebration pose, wearing only a pair of white Calvin Klein hip briefs.The billboard has been a landmark in New York's SoHo neighbourhood for 24 years. Spanning roughly five storeys in height and a quarter of a city block in width, it has featured models, actors, singers, athletes and other celebrities over the years. Bellingham's appearance puts him in the company of names such as Bad Bunny, Jeremy Allen White and Justin Bieber.His selection also reflects the growing reach of football in the United States, which co-hosted the World Cup with Mexico and Canada. Bellingham became a social media sensation during the summer tournament, attracting attention for his performances on the pitch and his appearance."We were just in the area, and then my little sister, she was like, 'I got to see the Jude Bellingham poster' -- especially after they beat Mexico in the World Cup, right?" store manager George Lozano, was quoted as saying by news agency AFP."I personally wouldn't think (most Americans) would recognize him. I think it's still growing. It's growing in terms of the US... support for football. But I think now this would definitely help, right?"Not everyone who stopped to see the billboard was familiar with Bellingham. French tourist Roxane Marin, 33, said she liked the England midfielder but that he was not her favourite player."I like him but he's not my favorite," said Marin, who helped steer England to a famous 6-4 victory over France in the third-place playoff with an inspired 98th-minute solo spectacular."I watch football, but I can't remember if I saw that match," she said, as quoted by AFP.Marin said she had come across the billboard by chance, "but I think there are people who come on purpose."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nations League: How do Northern Ireland replace 'perfect player' Jamie Donley for Hungary visit?
articles.summary: With Jamie Donley suspended for Northern Ireland's Nations League visit to Hungary on Tuesday night, manager Michael O'Neill has a decision to make around a starting striker.
articles.body:
With six of his starting outfield players against Ukraine on Saturday night having gone into the game a yellow card away from suspension, it was always likely that Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill would need to reshuffle his team for the Nations League Group B2 finale in Hungary.

That the player who picked up the booking ended up being Jamie Donley, however, has presented the boss with something of a selection conundrum.

The Tottenham Hotspur forward, currently on loan at Luton Town, has started the side's past 10 games at centre-forward, a different role to the deeper position he has more usually occupied in his club career.

With O'Neill having circled through traditional number nine options such as Dion Charles, Jamie Reid and Lee Bonis since returning to the job four years ago, it feels as if Donley has made the shirt his own since being handed the start against Luxembourg 12 months ago.

While the manager has pushed back on the idea that Donley is playing out of position at international level, the one-game ban is certainly an untimely one with the former Leyton Orient and Oxford United loanee's hold-up play in particular against Ukraine showing how much he has grown into the role.

After the 21-year-old had a goal chalked off by the video assistant referee (VAR) on Saturday, he has still scored just once from open play for his country, but there is a growing appreciation that he is asked to bring much more than just goals to the team.

"He's been such a good player for us. Even without the goals, the way he holds the ball up and spreads the play, his movement is just so good. Playing balls in the air, he pins the defender so well," said Fulham midfielder Shea Charles.

"He's got better every game and he's like the perfect player for us."

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC One NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

There is no obvious like-for-like replacement in O'Neill's squad for a game in which they need a draw to secure promotion to Nations League A for the first time.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill pulled out of the double-header through injury last week, with Josh Magennis, Callum Marshall and the uncapped pair of Eoin Kenny and Braiden Graham the other strikers in the travelling party.

Similar to the original ask of Donley, there is also an option to move a wide or deeper player such as Isaac Price or Paddy Kelly into a central striking role.

With only three days between games, however, there has been little time to work on such a plan to replace a player whose four Spurs appearances all came under Ange Postecoglou in the 2023-24 season.

"There are other things we can do. We can change the shape a little bit, play with two front players," said O'Neill, who himself is suspended for the game after two bookings and will watch from the stands.

"There's a number of things that we will look at. Obviously the time between the games makes that somewhat more difficult in terms of preparation.

"We'll find hopefully the right player that can first of all fit into what we want to do, but obviously secondly give the opposition some problems as well."

'No point' in NI playing for a draw in Hungary

The 'manager's dream' who has put NI one game from history

Devlin nets winner as NI top Nations League group

'Me and Marshy will probably play rock, paper, scissors'

Nobody in O'Neill's squad has more international caps or goals than Stevenage striker Magennis.

But while the 36-year-old has started 11 games in League One this season, it has been more than three years since he last did so at international level.

"My role has obviously changed since I've come into the squad," said the player with 94 international appearances and 12 goals to his name.

"If Michael wants to play with the target man and with experience, obviously, he's going to go for me. If he wants a like-for-like, he's probably going to go with Marshy [Callum Marshall]. So, me and Marshy will probably play rock, paper, scissors.

"Jamie brings so much to the team, but I don't think there's going to be a drastic downfall if one of us has to step in for us. I think the competition for places in the squad for us is absolutely brilliant and if you get that opportunity, you've just got to take it."

articles.title: Jesus Owono: Gerard Pique says goalkeeper did not deserve 12-match ban for tackle which resulted in death of Jesus de Miguel
articles.summary: FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique says goalkeeper Jesus Owono did not deserve the 12-match suspension he received following his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
articles.body:
FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique says goalkeeper Jesus Owono did not deserve the 12-match suspension he received following his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with De Miguel late on in the second-tier match between Andorra and Tenerife on 2 November.

De Miguel died the following day, aged 30, and a disciplinary committee from the Spanish football federation confirmed Owono's ban last week.

In a video posted on social media, Pique said players past and present, plus coaches and other goalkeepers, felt the incident was "an accident".

The former Spain and Barcelona defender added: "I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened."

Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision

Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision gets 12-game ban

The 12-match suspension was the maximum punishment Owono, 25, could have received, as the disciplinary committee could only consider the offence on the pitch and not "the tragic outcome of the incident".

Following the decision, Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera said he accepted the regulations do not specifically account for what happened, but acknowledged the ban "might feel light".

Pique also highlighted a recent on-field incident in Spain, when Albacete winger Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell midfielder Quadri Liameed in the head during a Spanish second division match.

Nigerian Liameed was knocked unconscious but was later discharged from hospital following medical checks, while Spaniard Corpas was shown a straight red card and handed a three-match ban.

"Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches," Pique said.

"With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?"

Owono has withdrawn from Equatorial Guinea's squad for Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Zimbabwe this month, and Pique said it was unlikely he would return to action as soon as his suspension is served.

He added: "Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to compete.

"No sanction is going to bring [De Miguel] back to us."

articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything Team tell you all you need to know about the Nations League quarter-final draw.
articles.body:
The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however a win or draw for Northern Ireland against Hungary would see them top Group B2 and be promoted to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

articles.title: The Mike Ashley relegations pre Newcastle United takeover and lessons to be learnt
articles.summary: I hold my hands up that I was guilty of a bit of an oversight during The Mag Podcast last week. “Those who do not learn from the past are doomed to repeat it...
articles.body:
I hold my hands up that I was guilty of a bit of an oversight during The Mag Podcast last week.

"Those who do not learn from the past are doomed to repeat it" – George Santayana

I half remembered the quote above and threw it to my co-host Hutch on The Mag Pod to try and recite it verbatim, as he likes history and stuff like that.

There were two errors involved to be fair, me for putting him on the spot like that, and Hutch for being as thick as mince.

Jamie puts Hutch on the spot over Newcastle United's relegation history

Anyway, I've since found the appropriate wording and replicated as a starting point here, as a way of conveying what we've been doing on The Mag Pod as we tried to fill the ongoing international break. Basically, there has been some chatter and paranoia that the issues this Newcastle United side are facing this season could well lead to a relegation battle. If it does turn out that way, it won't be any of our first rodeos.

However, it's fair to say that many of those Mike Ashley era struggles ended fairly benignly, with the drop avoided. On occasions this was comfortably, at times it was squeaky, but it didn't really matter as long as you lived to fight another day. Unfortunately, there were exceptions.

So, to try and learn the lessons of history, we have used this round of podcasts to look at the Mike Ashley seasons where it went terribly wrong.

Late last week the first instalment ( Episode 16 ) dropped, as we took a walk through the chaotic 2008-09 season. The follow-up, reliving the relegation of 2015-16 ( Episode 17 ), which is out now.

These serve as both a wander through times gone by and a study in what we can learn.

Ideally, listeners may feel better about current circumstances in comparison with the poor decisions, awful form and careless business that led to highly avoidable seasons away from the Premier League under the previous regime.

Unfortunately there may be times when certain things ring true and we appear in real danger of breaking Mr Santayana's above rule.

There is a third instalment to come as well, but alas we are a bit wet behind the lugs to fully recount the demotion of 1988-89.

Instead, a slight change of tack is incoming where Thursday's edition (Episode 18) will see a review of the 2020-21 season, the final year before the Newcastle United takeover . This is to give a perspective on how far we have come, the impact of the considerable changes since and to hopefully make you all feel better you're no longer looking at Steve Bruce.

Spoiler alert, but the general overall conclusion of these editions is that more time and consideration is needed in the current circumstances, to really have a full and proper idea of how badly it may compare to some of our darker times. However, there are things in there that may very well resonate.

Please enjoy The Mag Podcast and we'd love your feedback on what we have done so far and suggestions for the future in the commenting section below.

articles.title: Is Vinicius Jr really back? Brazil star scores his first-ever national team hat-trick in under 20 mins after admitting he is only 'human'
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr shines for Brazil with his first international hat-trick in a friendly match against Singapore, showcasing his remarkable return to form after a challenging start to the season.
articles.body: Vinicius Jr needed barely 20 minutes to deliver the kind of performance Brazil have been waiting to see from him, scoring three times against Singapore to take his tally to five goals in two internationals. It marks an encouraging turnaround after a difficult start to the season at Real Madrid, where the forward admitted that his preparation had fallen short of his usual standards, although the quality of opposition means his return to form will be better judged when he resumes club duties.Vinicius Jr ends Brazil's year with first international hat-trickVinicius scored his first hat-trick for Brazil in Tuesday's 7-0 friendly victory over Singapore, completing all three goals inside the opening 20 minutes at the National Stadium.He opened the scoring in the ninth minute, controlling the ball inside the penalty area before turning and sending a low finish towards the right post. Six minutes later, Endrick supplied the assist for his second goal as Brazil broke forward on the counter-attack. Vinicius completed the hat-trick in the 20th minute, this time finishing after a pass from Estevao.It was a remarkably productive opening spell for the Real Madrid forward, who was substituted in the 59th minute after giving Brazil a commanding lead. Endrick, who started alongside him and played the full match, added the fourth shortly before half-time with a powerful left-footed effort from the edge of the penalty area. Estevao and Rayan also scored, while Singapore's Suhaimi put through his own net to complete the 7-0 result.The fixture was the first meeting between Brazil and Singapore, and the hosts were unable to offer much resistance. Singapore are ranked 149th in the world, making this a very different test from the matches Vinicius faces at the highest level of international football.That qualification matters, but so does the confidence the forward can take from the performance. His hat-trick followed a brace against Japan on November 14, when Brazil lost 3-2. Five goals across two matches have given him a strong finish to the international year, even if the two performances came in very different circumstances.A difficult start at Real Madrid made the goals more significantThe sudden burst of international scoring comes after Vinicius acknowledged that his performances at the beginning of the 2026-27 season had fallen below his own expectations.Speaking before the Singapore friendly, the 26-year-old offered a candid explanation for his lack of sharpness. “I trained less, I made mistakes, I’m human,” he said, accepting that his preparation had contributed to his early-season struggles.Brazil's unexpected early exit from the World Cup had taken an emotional toll, and Vinicius admitted that he prioritised rest and time with his family during the off-season instead of following his usual intensive conditioning programme. He recognised that the decision had affected his physical preparation and left him short of the sharpness expected at the start of a new campaign.There were other distractions. Transfer speculation involving rival clubs and uncertainty surrounding his contract renewal at the Bernabeu added to the pressure during the summer. The combination of those issues made the opening months more difficult, although Vinicius remained confident that there was enough time in the season to recover his best form.His three goals against Singapore do not settle the question of whether that recovery has begun. They do, however, offer a more encouraging indication than the performances that preceded them, particularly after he followed his brace against Japan with another three goals just three days later.Brazil's goalscoring run is encouraging, but the bigger test awaitsVinicius has never lacked the ability to produce decisive performances for Real Madrid. He has scored four competitive hat-tricks for the Spanish club: against Levante in 2022, Barcelona in the 2024 Spanish Super Cup final, Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League later that year, and Osasuna in LaLiga in 2024. His three goals against Singapore take his senior career hat-trick tally to five.The international milestone is nevertheless significant. Vinicius has often carried the expectation of being one of Brazil's leading attacking players, but his goalscoring record for the national team has not always reflected the influence he has established at club level. Scoring five times in two November fixtures gives him a welcome boost as Brazil close their 2026 campaign.The next question is whether he can carry that confidence back to Madrid. A hat-trick against Singapore is not proof that his earlier problems have disappeared, and the quality of opposition should temper any suggestion that he has already rediscovered his best level. But his admission about his preparation, followed by consecutive multi-goal performances for Brazil, provides a clearer picture of both what went wrong and what may be changing.Vinicius has acknowledged the mistakes behind his slow start. He now has five goals in two appearances to build on, with Brazil having completed their final match of 2026. The more demanding test comes when he returns to Real Madrid, where he will need to show that this renewed scoring touch can translate into consistent performances at club level.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother slams Portugal manager Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: Following an average 2026 FIFA World Cup performance and a below-par UEFA Nations League game, Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international...
articles.body:
Following an average 2026 FIFA World Cup performance and a below-par UEFA Nations League game , Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international soccer . Ronaldo was benched during Portugal's second UEFA Nations League game, following which there arose a certain miscommunication between him and Portugal's manager, Jorge Jesus.

After several more back-and-forth exchanges and a press conference, Ronaldo parted ways with the team . He was later fined and suspended from the team; Ronaldo announced his retirement and parted ways with the team after 23 years. A true legend, Ronaldo bid adieu to Portugal as their captain.

Later, after Portugal's 1-4 loss to Denmark, Jesus was asked about his thoughts on Ronaldo's absence and if he missed the legend . "Do I miss him? But what is there to miss? If he's no longer available for the national team, what exactly are we missing? (…) He no longer plays, he's no longer here, and he's already made his decision about his situation," he further added. (quotes translated via X's auto translate)

However, Ronaldo's retirement and departure from the Portugal team did not sit well with his mother . Recently, at a sporting event on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026, Dolores Aveiro was asked about her son's national team retirement. "Of course he was sad. They deceived him. And I'm sad, too. The defeat [against Denmark] was well-deserved. I was actually glad," she said (quotes via BBC).

Soon after, before Portugal's Nations League game against Wales in Cardiff, Jesus was asked for his thoughts on Aveiro's comments. "Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo's mother?" he said. "She is a lady I greatly respect – she suffered a lot to raise her children."

"I don't know when it's going to stop. If you guys ask the questions, I have to answer. If you ask about Ronaldo next year, I will answer," Jesus further answered when asked when questions about Ronaldo's retirement would stop.

Ronaldo, 41, spent over two decades with Portugal's national team and retired after a legendary career consisting of 234 games and 146 goals for his country.

articles.title: David Beckham Sues for $41 Million After His Fragrance is Sold in Gas Stations and Discount Stores
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — A dispute over the sale of David Beckham perfumes has struck a sour note with the soccer star turned style icon.
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — A dispute over the sale of David Beckham perfumes has struck a sour note with the soccer star turned style icon.

Beckham's commercial company is suing a beauty firm after his "luxury" fragrances were allegedly found for sale in discount stores and a gas station bargain bin.

DB Ventures has filed a claim in the New York Supreme Court against German beauty group Coty, which makes and distributes a range of Beckham-branded fragrances and toiletries. They include the Classic and Instinct lines and the eaux de toilette Intimately and Exquisite Leather.

The claim argues that Beckham's "world-renowned global brand is synonymous with excellence and refinement," and "David Beckham products are a symbol of everyday luxury."

"Imagine, then, the shock and dismay experienced when DB Ventures discovered that David Beckham products were being offered for sale in a gas station," the legal document says. "How could this possibly have happened? Desperation and greed."

Lawyers for DB Ventures allege that Beckham-branded products "ended up in the bargain bin inside a gas station" and at British budget retailer Poundland, "allowing the product to be sold for dollar store prices and associating the David Beckham brand with cheap, discount products."

DB Ventures is seeking at least $41 million in damages for breach of its licensing agreement.

Coty has asked a judge to dismiss the lawsuit, which was filed in April. The company argues that New York courts have no jurisdiction in the case, and says DB Ventures is using the claim to "manufacture its early exit" from its licensing deal and hand over the Beckham contracts to another firm, Interparfums.

The company told The Associated Press on Tuesday that "Coty strongly disputes the claims and has asked the court to dismiss them. As this is an ongoing legal matter, we will not comment further."

DB Ventures' parent company, U.S. entertainment and lifestyles firm Authentic Brands, declined to comment.

Beckham, who played for a number of clubs including Manchester United and Real Madrid and captained the England men's national team, parlayed success on the pitch into a lucrative business career that includes co-ownership of soccer team Inter Miami. He was knighted last year by King Charles III, becoming Sir David.

He also has had a very public persona as a fashion model, "Bend It Like Beckham" movie muse and husband of Spice Girl-turned-fashion designer Victoria "Posh Spice" Beckham. The couple have four children.

The Sunday Times Rich List earlier this year estimated the Beckhams' wealth at almost 1.2 billion pounds ($1.58 billion).

articles.title: Miami Dolphins’ Most Valuable Player | Week Ten | Youth
articles.summary: Chris Johnson has 59-yard interception return for touchdown against Colts.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins have been going through a bit of a youth-movement this season, in case you haven't heard. They're the youngest team in the National Football League by a wide margin — with an average age of just over 25 years at the start of the season. They've also had the most snaps taken by rookie players out of any NFL team this season — leading the Cleveland Browns by a comfortable amount.

That emphasis on developing young players is paying off for the Dolphins in a major way. While the team is currently struggling in the standings — winning just one game on the year so far — their rookies are taking their lumps and learning the ropes at an expedited pace. That should help the team progress much quicker than most anticipate, while keeping their future cap situation in the good (and cheap) place.

Miami Dolphins Week Nine MVP – Cornerback Chris Johnson

One young player who has been excelling in Jeff Halfey's defensive scheme is rookie first-rounder Chris Johnson. Miami's young cornerback has two interceptions on the season after nabbing one against Daniel Jones of the Colts on Sunday. He returned that interception 59-yards for a touchdown — Miami's first pick-6 on the year. In addition to his two interceptions, Johnson also has a forced fumble during his rookie campaign.

Following the game, Johnson spoke about how coaching helped him make his stellar play on Sunday.

"Definitely felt good. Really just reading my keys. Once the quarterback scrambles, he's looking to get the ball out of his hands. That's kind of something we talked about throughout the week. When we get him off-schedule, it's an opportunity. Really just making the most of my opportunity in that situation."

articles.title: Piqué Criticizes 12-Game Ban for Andorra Goalkeeper after Collision That Led to Player's Death
articles.summary: MADRID (AP) — Andorra owner Gerard Piqué has questioned the 12-game ban handed to goalkeeper Jesús Owono following a collision that resulted in another player's death, saying the punishment should have been based on the challenge rather than its tragic consequences.
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — Andorra owner Gerard Piqué has questioned the 12-game ban handed to goalkeeper Jesús Owono following a collision that resulted in another player's death, saying the punishment should have been based on the challenge rather than its tragic consequences.

Piqué, a former Spain and Barcelona defender, criticized the sanction in a video posted on TikTok late Monday, two weeks after Owono's on-field collision with 30-year-old Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel in a second-division match.

De Miguel, who was nicknamed "Demi", died the following morning.

Piqué said "there is no sanction that could give us Demi back," and noted that it will take more than 12 games for Owono to be ready to play again. But he didn't think the punishment was fair to the goalkeeper.

"I truly believe imposing the maximum suspension on Jesús for this challenge puts him in a position he doesn't deserve, because he is not to blame for everything that happened," Piqué said.

"What this sanction does is make it look like he was responsible for the consequences of what happened. The sanction should have been for his action, not for the consequences."

Piqué cited a challenge in another match that brought a three-game suspension, and recalled his own collision with Barcelona teammate Víctor Valdés in 2012. He said players, former players and coaches had described the Owono incident as an accident.

The disciplinary committee that punished Owono — who was sent off after the collision — said the goalkeeper used "excessive force."

De Miguel was chasing a high ball in midfield when he was struck in the chest by Owono, who rushed far outside his area, near the end of the Nov. 2 match in Tenerife. De Miguel suffered cardiac arrest following the collision.

Owono issued a statement through his club expressing his grief and offering his condolences to De Miguel's family.

Police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely.

Last week, Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again.

articles.body: El entrenador del Tenerife, Álvaro Cervera, ha respondido a Gerard Piqué en la rueda de prensa previa al partido de Copa que los chicharreros jugarán contra el Badajoz. El máximo accionista del Andorra comentó ayer que "imponerle la sanción máxima pone a Jesús en una situación que no se merece porque él no es el culpable de que todo esto haya pasado. Mi reflexión en todo esto es que lo que hacen estos 12 partidos es culpabilizarlo de unas consecuencias de las que él no tuvo la culpa". "No he visto el vídeo de Piqué, pero he escuchado las declaraciones. Me imagino que él, como máximo accionista del Andorra, está en su papel y tiene que defender a sus jugadores y a su club, y así lo hace", comenzó diciendo el míster del Tete. Y prosiguió: "Ha dicho que se castigan las consecuencias y no la acción, ¿no? En mi ámbito cercano, fuera del fútbol, tengo gente que opina de diferente manera respecto a estos hechos... Pero creo que él debería volver a ver la acción. No me he pronunciado públicamente ni lo voy a hacer, pero creo que se podía haber evitado; no creo que sea una acción que veamos todos los días, como parece que dice él".

articles.title: Updated Bowl Projections and 2026 CFP Bracket Predictions for Week 12
articles.summary: The 2026-27 College Football Playoff (CFP) picture continues to materialize. While the CFP committee won't update its rankings until 9 p.m. ET on Tuesday, the latest AP poll dropped on Monday afternoon.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 College Football Playoff (CFP) picture continues to materialize. While the CFP committee won't update its rankings until 9 p.m. ET on Tuesday, the latest AP poll dropped on Monday afternoon.

The poll release was pushed back from Sunday due to a rescheduled game between Mississippi and Oklahoma, which took place on Sunday afternoon.

While there aren't any real surprises in the latest poll, there's still some uncertainty about the playoff picture heading into Week 12. Let's take a look at what's ahead and make some updated predictions for this year's CFP bracket.

As previously noted, there weren't any shocking surprises in Week 11. We didn't see another No. 1 fall, as Georgia left no doubt about its status as a title contender while rolling Missouri 48-21.

Indiana managed to knock off an ascending USC team, 27-13, while Utah managed to stay unbeaten by outlasting Arizona 40-39. UCLA also remained undefeated by slogging through a 22-14 game against Illinois in the rain.

The one significant upset we saw was Florida's 21-14 win over the previously 11th-ranked Kentucky Wildcats. We nearly saw another major upset, though Texas managed to battle back against LSU.

The Tigers had a 21-13 lead over the Longhorns heading into the fourth quarter, and they seemed destined to keep their CFP hopes alive. However, Arch Manning overcame a three-interception outing to deliver a thrilling game-winning drive.

Manning found Raleek Brown for the go-ahead score with mere seconds remaining to keep Texas in the CFP field:

The loss was LSU's fourth and ended the playoff hopes of Lane Kiffin's squad.

Updated CFP Bowl and Bracket Predictions

Next year, the CFP will expand to 24 teams, making this the final year of the 12-team format. The final playoff selection will be similar to last year's format, with minor changes.

Notably, Notre Dame is guaranteed to make the playoff with a top-12 finish. This means that if the Irish finish in the No. 12 spot, they won't drop out to make room for the top-ranked Group of Six conference champion.

The top G6 team will automatically make the playoff, while the top four power conference champions will also earn automatic bids—though they won't receive automatic byes, as was the case a couple of years ago. For now, we'll project Boise State as the top G6 champion and Georgia, UCLA, Utah, and Miami as the champions of their respective conferences.

Conference championship week, which will begin in early December, could shake things up, of course.

Barring a major upset, we shouldn't see many changes to the playoff field in Week 12, as the schedule is largely devoid of matchups between top contenders. That doesn't mean, however, we won't see Tennessee stumble against LSU, Indiana lose to Washington or UCLA falter against Michigan.

If there's one thing we've learned during the 2026 season, it's that no outcome is guaranteed, especially when conference rivals get involved.

The prediction here, though, is that the CFP picture will remain largely unchanged after Week 12.

articles.title: Wayne Rooney: Ex-Manchester United captain considered taking own life during playing career
articles.summary: Wayne Rooney says he considered taking his own life during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up".
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains references to suicide

Wayne Rooney says he was "contemplating suicide" during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up".

The former England captain joined United from Everton in 2004 and went on to become the club's record goalscorer, with 253 goals in 559 appearances.

But Rooney, speaking with Gabby Logan on the Life at the Midpoint podcast , external , detailed his struggles off the pitch when eldest son Kai, who is now 17, was a baby.

"When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink," said Rooney, when asked about the lowest point in his life.

"This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise."

The 41-year-old went on to explain how he "struggled to deal with it all" and, after opening up to his wife Coleen and his mother, knew he "needed help to get through it".

"I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with," he added.

"I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well.

"I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. I just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops.

"I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, [I] really struggled with it."

Rooney, who scored 53 goals in 120 England appearances, was recently named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and is currently appearing on reality TV show I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here.

He helped United win five Premier League titles, the Champions League, Europa League, FA Cup and three EFL Cups before leaving them to return to the Toffees in 2017.

But the former forward said he learned to mask his feelings during his lowest moments.

"You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," Rooney added.

"Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that.

"I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married.

"It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't.

"It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.

"Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it."

articles.title: El Real Madrid lucha contra sus dos caras: "Un equipo que quiere luchar por títulos no puede tener altibajos"
articles.standfirst: El conjunto blanco quiere sacarse ante el Inter de Milán la espina clavada frente al Badalona
articles.summary: El conjunto blanco quiere sacarse ante el Inter de Milán la espina clavada frente al Badalona
articles.body: El Real Madrid se enfrenta este miércoles (18:45 horas) al Inter de Milán en plena búsqueda de su identidad. El equipo dirigido por Pau Quesada está mostrando dos caras bien diferenciadas, dando la menos amable en Liga, donde ha cedido tres empates y una derrota en 11 partidos (siendo el segundo equipo más goleado) y en Champions, donde se mantiene invicto y aspira seriamente al top4 continental. "Buscamos no tener ups and downs, tener ese balance que requiere un equipo que quiere luchar por títulos. Las jugadoras son conscientes de eso y desde el staff tenemos que dar esas herramientas a las jugadoras. Hay fases que parece que vas a ganar fácil y luego hay dos o tres jugadas que te lo complican. Sin embargo, en Champions sí que somos capaces de hacer ese balance defensivo. Es algo que debemos trabajar para ser consistentes", analizó el técnico, con el foco puesto ya en el duelo ante el Inter. "Es un equipo que hace muy bien el bloque y las situaciones de atacar la profundidad. Es un rival incómodo. Tenemos que encontrar la versión ofrecida ante el Paris FC", añadió. El valenciano insiste en la necesidad de madurar un estilo de juego que ha evolucionado esta temporada. "Desde el año pasado estamos inculcando una presión muy alta, tanto en Liga como en Europa; un dinamismo, verticalidad tras robo, y lo queremos no sólo en grandes escenarios sino en el día a día queremos ser el mismo Real Madrid. Tenemos que ser nosotras independientemente del rival", apuntó. El equipo blanco, que rompió una racha negativa de diez partidos seguidos encajando ante el Paris FC hace una semana, volvió a encajar tres el sábado frente al Badalona. "El año pasado logramos 25 porterías a cero. Creo que fuimos el tercer equipo de Europa que más logró. Estamos metiendo toda nuestra energía en este aspecto para que ellas tengan esas herramientas. Si quieres luchar por títulos tienes que ser un equipo cada vez más completo. Tenemos que mejorar en esa contundencia en el área, ya lo hemos hecho a nivel de generar volumen de ocasiones", analizó Quesada. Ahondando en el plano defensivo, Quesada volvió a valorar la irrupción de Laia López en la portería blanca. "Era ya nuestra portera proyecto. Es muy reactiva, para mucho. En situaciones bajo palos es muy buena y con balón genera ventaja. Dos goles ante el Paris FC salen de una construcción de ella. Tenemos que intentar ayudarla a que vaya creciendo, pero es una portera de rendimiento inmediato", sentenció.

articles.title: Los aliados sorpresa por la final del Mundial en España: Diallo y un demócrata de EE.UU. que puede aguarle la fiesta a Infantino
articles.standfirst: UEFA confía en el presidente de la Federación Francesa para ganar las elecciones de marzo a la FIFA, pero casi más en el candidato opositor a Trump, Jamie Raskin
articles.summary: Jamie Raskin está dispuesto a llamar a declarar
articles.body: La final del Mundial de 2030 aún no tiene dueño. Las dudas bajo el mandato actual de la FIFA son razonables. Marruecos no se lanzaría a construir el Gran Estadio Hassan II con capacidad para 135.000 espectadores si no viera que alberga opciones. Para una Liga nacional que hace aguas por todas partes, con sospechas de corrupción arbitral y violencia en los estadios, un proyecto de esa envergadura no se entiende. Para España, aunque no hay nada decidido, garantizarse la final bien en Madrid o Barcelona y terminar con esta incertidumbre a corto y medio plazo pasa por dos nombres: Philippe Diallo, el candidato elegido por la UEFA para presentarse a las elecciones del próximo 18 de marzo en Rabat, casualidades de la vida, y un aliado inesperado en Estados Unidos, Jamie Raskin, el demócrata de mayor rango en el Comité Judicial de la Cámara de Representantes desde enero de 2025 y que ahora está más fuerte que nunca como dique de contención a Donald Trump tras ganar su partido la mayoría en la Cámara. El caso es que su frente contra el presidente de Estados Unidos va a salpicar a Infantino desde que tome posesión del cargo el próximo mes de enero. La UEFA es consciente de que era casi de obligado cumplimiento presentar un candidato tras promover desde dentro esta alternativa. Casi antes de sonar la campana, el máximo organismo europeo ha anunciado a este ex boxeador y ex futbolista, abogado que, como presidente de la Federación Francesa, mostró su apoyo a Infantino por carta, eso sí, antes de que se destapara el escándalo del proyecto de vender parte del Mundial a empresas privadas ligadas a la familia Trump. El problema es que no está nada claro que Diallo, tras no dar con un perfil mucho más influyente, saque más apoyos que Infantino el próximo 18 de marzo pese a que UEFA garantice una final en el viejo continente. Por eso mismo, Ceferin ha judicializado ya el proyecto FIFA Forward Enterprise presentando solicitudes ante tribunales federales en Nueva York, Florida y Colorado con el fin de obtener documentos, correos y modelos financieros del banco JPMorgan y al fondo de inversión Thrive Capital, fundado por Joshua Kushner (hermano de Jared Kushner, yerno de Donald Trump). FIFA trató de frenar esa maniobra pero un juzgado de Nueva York ha dado vía libre a esos documentos. Es en esta vía donde UEFA alberga esperanzas de derrocar a Infantino. Esos documentos irían a parar ahora a la denuncia presentada en Suiza contra el presidente de la FIFA por mala gestión delictiva. Una sentencia en este sentido va para largo, así que la idea es que en este primer proceso haya tiempo para obtener munición suficiente como para poner en cuestión la gestión del presidente. A la UEFA, los ciudadanos de Estados Unidos le han dado otro empujón en su intento de derrocar a Infantino, aunque su enemigo fuera otro. Las presiones desde España, como la de Alberto Tomé, Director general de Deportes de la Comunidad de Madrid, que habló con MARCA en el seno del 'Business Sport Forum' para pedir coherencia a la FIFA siempre ayudan. También la buena impresión que han dejado el Bernabéu y el Camp Nou en la visita reciente de los emisarios de FIFA, pero lamentablemente la partida se juega mucho más arriba y Marruecos tiene buenos aliados. Y es ahí donde entra Jamie Raskin, que lleva tiempo desconfiando de la complicidad de Infantino con Trump. La FIFA ha salido airoso hasta el momento, pero ahora será más complicado tras el triunfo arrollador de los demócratas en las midterms que le otorgan el control tanto de la Cámara de Representantes como del Senado de Estados Unidos. Al asumir la presidencia del comité en enero de 2027, Raskin tiene mucha más capacidad para poner en aprietos a Trump y, en consecuencia, a Infantino. Ahora, el presidente de la FIFA puede verse obligado a declarar bajo juramento. El congresista demócrata sostiene que Infantino pudo ofrecer ventajas económicas y tratos de favor a Trump a cambio de otros intereses ajenos a la FIFA. UEFA espera que desde enero esta ofensiva pueda influir en las elecciones a la presidencia de la FIFA. Medir el impacto es complicado, los apoyos suelen ser casi inamovibles e Infantino tiene el voto de confederaciones como la africana (CAF), a la espera de lo que pueda rascar Diallo, o la sudamericana (Conmebol), así que UEFA podría volver a su empeño en forzar la dimisión del presidente de la FIFA como cuando se destapó el escándalo del Mundial. La sensación, en cualquier caso, es que España va a necesitar toda la ayuda de la UEFA para una decisión que suele conocerse dos o tres años antes de que arranque el Mundial, por lo que se entra ya en el periodo decisivo. Y el propio Louzán, que ha pedido celeridad a la FIFA, lo sabe.

articles.title: Revés del Tribunal Supremo a LaLiga por su acuerdo con CVC
articles.standfirst: La patronal asegura en un comunicado que el Proyecto LALIGA Impulso continúa plenamente vigente y desarrollándose con normalidad
articles.summary: La patronal asegura en un comunicado que el Proyecto LALIGA Impulso continúa plenamente vigente y desarrollándose con normalidad
articles.body: El Tribunal Supremo ha inadmitido el recurso de casación interpuesto por LaLiga contra la sentencia de la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid, que confirmó la nulidad del acuerdo adoptado por la Asamblea General de LaLiga para aprobar la operación con el fondo de inversión CVC, según ha anunciado el propio club blanco en un comunicado. De esta forma, la sentencia ya es firme y condena a la Liga al pago de las costas del recurso. "El Tribunal Supremo confirma así la firmeza de la declaración judicial de nulidad de un acuerdo de extraordinaria trascendencia económica, adoptado sin que los clubes dispusieran de información suficiente para conocer y valorar el alcance, el impacto y las consecuencias de las modificaciones introducidas en la operación", apunta el club blanco en su comunicado. El Madrid resalta en su comunicado que "resulta especialmente significativo que el propio Tribunal Supremo señale que LaLiga, en su recurso, pretendía sustituir el criterio de la Audiencia Provincial por el suyo propio e interesado". "El Real Madrid considera que esta resolución constituye un nuevo y contundente respaldo judicial a su defensa de los derechos de los clubes frente a actuaciones de LaLiga, que vulneran las garantías que deben regir el funcionamiento de sus órganos de gobierno. El Real Madrid continuará defendiendo los derechos e intereses de los clubes y el respeto a la legalidad, la transparencia y el buen gobierno del fútbol español", concluye el club blanco en su comunicado. 1. No afecta al Proyecto LALIGA Impulso La resolución no afecta a la validez ni a la vigencia del Proyecto LALIGA Impulso con CVC, aprobado posteriormente por la Asamblea General del 10 de diciembre de 2021. Las cuestiones de fondo de este proyecto se han abordado en un procedimiento judicial independiente, en el que la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid desestimó las pretensiones de los dos clubes demandantes, Real Madrid CF y Athletic Club, y confirmó la validez de los acuerdos adoptados. 2. Se limita a cuestiones formales muy concretas La sentencia de la Audiencia Provincial recurrida por LALIGA se centraba exclusivamente en aspectos formales de la Asamblea de agosto de 2021: * Convocatoria: la Audiencia Provincial consideró que la Asamblea se convocó correctamente y que los defectos alegados por los demandantes, Real Madrid CF y Athletic Club, no eran suficientes para invalidar el acuerdo. * Derecho de información: también concluyó que la información puesta a disposición por LALIGA a sus miembros fue completa y suficiente. Pese a ello, la Audiencia Provincial desestimó el recurso de LALIGA por un único motivo: consideró que la incorporación de una aclaración sobre la no afectación de la operación a los clubes y SAD no adheridos suponía una modificación sustancial del orden del día que los asistentes no pudieron estudiar previamente, vulnerando así su derecho de información. 3. El Tribunal Supremo no se ha pronunciado sobre el fondo del asunto Frente a lo señalado en algunas informaciones, el Tribunal Supremo no ha dictado una sentencia que confirme o ratifique los razonamientos de la Audiencia Provincial. Su providencia se limita a inadmitir el recurso de casación por no considerar suficientemente acreditado el interés casacional exigido, sin entrar a examinar las cuestiones de fondo planteadas por LALIGA. La sentencia ha sido objeto de casación por el Real Madrid, estando pendiente de la admisión por el supremo del mencionado Recurso LALIGA respeta las resoluciones judiciales y seguirá defendiendo, por las vías legales correspondientes, la actuación de sus órganos de gobierno y los acuerdos respaldados por la mayoría de sus clubes. El Proyecto LALIGA Impulso continúa plenamente vigente y desarrollándose con normalidad, contribuyendo a la modernización y el crecimiento del fútbol profesional español.

articles.title: FA want to host Nations League finals in England
articles.summary: England could host the Nations League finals this season after Football Association officials register their interest.
articles.body:
England could host the Nations League finals this season after Football Association officials registered their interest.

The semi-final and finals of the competition, due to take place in June, are held in one country.

As well as England, it is understood that Spain and France have also contacted Uefa to register their interest in hosting the final four games, including the bronze medal match, which will run between 9-13 June.

The FA, it is understood, is still discussing potential venues with some doubt over whether Wembley would be available. The only publicly announced Wembley events in June are two concerts by singer Sam Fender, although these are for after the Nations League.

Since the tournament began in 2019, England have never held the finals, with Portugal, Italy, Netherlands and Germany the hosts to date.

Generally, only nations who reach the last four of the Nations League are considered to host the latter stages.

Thomas Tuchel's team will be seeded in Friday's draw for the quarter-finals following their euphoric 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid, which secured top place in the group.

They could face Belgium, Netherlands, Denmark or Norway in March in the next round before June's finals.

If the FA's bid is successful, it will provide the governing body with an opportunity to host a mini-tournament before Euro 2028, which will be held in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

articles.title: Afcon 2027: Senegal become first side to qualify but Nigeria struggle in qualifiers
articles.summary: Senegal become the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, while Egypt miss the chance to join them and Nigeria suffer another setback.
articles.body:
Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) before Egypt and Ivory Coast were among five sides who missed out on the chance to join them.

Led by new head coach Patrick Vieira, Senegal had moved to the brink of a place at the finals by beating Sudan 4-2 on Monday, and the Teranga Lions had their ticket confirmed with two games to spare in Group J when Mozambique secured a 1-0 victory away against Ethiopia.

Algeria, DR Congo, Egypt and the Ivorians could have progressed with away wins, but all four sides failed to pick up three points.

Brighton forward Yankuba Minteh was on target as The Gambia came from behind to lead Ivory Coast 2-1 in Group C, but Christ Inao Oulai grabbed a stoppage-time equaliser after Scorpions striker Muhammed Badamosi was sent off in the 90th minute.

Egypt were held to a goalless draw in Malawi, Sierra Leone claimed a late point against the Congolese and Algeria suffered a 3-0 defeat in Togo.

Angola beat South Sudan 1-0 in Juba and would have qualified had Egypt claimed all three points in the other match in Group B.

Cameroon, Senegal and Benin close in on Afcon 2027 qualification

Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

Five more sides, including Morocco and Cameroon, could join Senegal in booking a spot at next year's finals in East Africa as the fourth round of fixtures culminates on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Nigeria are in danger of missing out on Afcon for the first time since 2017 after the Super Eagles failed to beat tournament co-hosts Tanzania.

Tunisia, who have appeared at a record 17 consecutive editions of the tournament, could also be absent after their winless start in Group H was extended with a 1-1 draw in Libya.

The final two rounds of qualifiers will be held in March next year, with Afcon 2027 scheduled to be held in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July.

Seven-time Afcon winners Egypt knew victory in Lilongwe could take them to the finals but were frustrated by an inspired second-half showing from Malawi goalkeeper George Chikooka.

After Pharaohs captain Mohamed Salah had hit the outside of the post from a tight angle, Chikooka denied Trezeguet and Haissem Hassan before also making fine stops from Mohamed Hany and Ibrahim Adel in stoppage time.

Egypt move on to eight points in Group B, two points behind Angola after Miro's first-half effort secured a 1-0 victory for the Palancas Negras in Juba.

There was drama as Ivory Coast salvaged a draw in Bakau through Inao Oulai's 98th-minute goal, which denied The Gambia a third win in Group C.

The Ivorians lead the pool on 10 points, with The Gambia on seven and Ghana on six following the Black Stars' back-to-back wins over Somalia.

DR Congo appeared on track to progress from Group E as Junior Kadile gave the Leopards a half-time lead in their away tie against Sierra Leone, but Alie Conteh netted in the 94th minute for the West Africans.

And Togo moved a point behind Group I leaders Algeria after a strong first-half showing in Lome, with two goals from Thibault Klidje before Kennedy Boateng's powerful header secured a 3-0 win over the 2019 champions from North Africa.

Nigeria's hopes of progressing suffered another blow as Eric Chelle's men drew 0-0 with Tanzania in Zanzibar.

With East Africans Tanzania already assured of a spot at the finals, as co-hosts, Nigeria are competing with Guinea-Bissau for just one qualification spot available in Group L.

And Guinea-Bissau established a three-point advantage over the Super Eagles as goals from Mama Balde and Mauro Rodrigues gave them a 2-0 home win over Madagascar.

After falling to a 3-0 defeat in Bissau in September, even maximum points in the final two rounds of qualifiers may not be enough for three-time continental champions Nigeria to reach the tournament.

In another section with just one qualifying berth, Tunisia are rock bottom of Group H on three points after a fractious 1-1 draw with Libya in Tripoli.

Anis Ben Slimane capitalised on a defensive error to fire the Carthage Eagles ahead in the third minute, but Ezoo El Mariamy levelled for the hosts from 12 yards in first-half injury time.

Tunisia's players and officials vehemently protested against the decision to award a foul after El Mariamy tussled with defender Ghaith Zaalouni and collided with goalkeeper Aymen Dahmen, delaying the penalty for several minutes.

The visitors then had their own claims for a spot-kick turned down after a similar coming together between Mohamed Belhadj Mahmoud and Libya keeper Ayman Al Tihar, with Tunisian players surrounding Beninois referee Adissa Ligali and his assistants at the full-time whistle.

Elsewhere, South Africa returned to the top of Group D with a 2-1 win over co-hosts Kenya , and Lesotho recorded a surprise 2-1 win over Gabon in Group A, leaving Morocco needing just a point from their match against Niger to go through.

articles.title: Arsenal transfer news: David Raya, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie close to finalising new contracts
articles.summary: David Raya and Jurrien Timber were about to enter the last 18 months of their Arsenal contracts; both players have rubberstamped their statuses as the best players in their positions in Europe; Piero Hincapie only joined Arsenal on a permanent basis last summer
articles.body:
Sky Sports News reported on Monday that midfielder Declan Rice has verbally agreed a new contract and champions Arsenal are set to also tie down Raya, Timber and Hincapie.

Raya's current deal expires in 2028 but he is on the verge of signing an extension after establishing himself as one of the world's best goalkeepers since joining Arsenal, initially on loan from Brentford, in 2023.

Defender Timber joined Arsenal from Ajax in the same summer as Raya and his current contract is due to expire in 2028.

Speaking about reports he had agreed a new Arsenal deal, following the Netherlands 5-0 Nations League defeat against Germany on Monday, Timber told ESPN Netherlands : "Those are good reports. They are definitely on the right track! It will all work out, yes.

"If I extend, hopefully a few years will be added. You know better than I do. I feel at home here, I'm enjoying myself. Quinten [Timber - his twin brother at Crystal Palace] is in London now too, so we are doing well.

"I think we will definitely still be competing for trophies in the coming years. The club is happy with me as well, so that is good too. It all looks good."

Defender Hincapie - an initial loan signing from Bayer Leverkusen in 2025 - is also in talks over an extension with Arsenal confident he too will commit his long-term future to the club.

Arsenal on a contract roll - who else could get new deals?

Arsenal are going through a major contract renewal surge at the moment. Mikel Arteta has one of the best squads in Europe and - after the Arsenal manager committed to new terms earlier this year - he wants to keep it that way.

Other Arsenal players to commit to new contracts in the last 18 months include Bukayo Saka, Gabriel and William Saliba - while the long-term futures of high-profile youngsters such as Ethan Nwaneri, Myles Lewis-Skell y and Max Dowman have been secured.

In Timber, Raya and Declan Rice, Arsenal have ended any speculation about players moving towards the final year of their contract. The days of the early 2010s where Arsenal were sweating over the long-term futures of their major stars is clearly over.

But there are a still a handful of players who still have their futures hanging in the balance. The most pressing is captain Martin Odegaard , who has become a key player again after an injury-hit campaign last term.

The Norwegian midfielder, whose contract expires in 2028, has publicly revealed his desire to stay, but will a deal be struck before more questions and doubts start coming?

Another player entering the last 18 months of his contract is Kai Havertz - who again has had doubters and injury issues in recent years. With Arsenal's attack a clear area that needs to be improved, does one of Arteta's highest-paid players get another bump?

Ben White is another player whose contract expires in 2028, though the club have the option of an extra year extension on his deal. With Jurrien Timber, Ezri Konsa and Cristhian Mosquera also available for Arsenal in his position - a decision on his long-term future will also need to come soon.

The same contract expiry date also applies for Mikel Merino , who is struggling for regular minutes in a stacked Arsenal midfield that includes Lewis-Skelly, Bruno Guimaraes and Martin Zubimendi, who looks set to stay and fight for his place.

When Arsenal don't see a long-term vision for a player, they make it fairly clear when they let them go into the final year of their contracts. Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Jesus found that out, despite all three playing plenty of minutes across the season.

So what do Arsenal do with Odegaard, Havertz, White and Merino?

articles.title: India beat 10-man Pakistan 2–1 in Dhaka final to complete three-peat and lift record 10th SAFF crown
articles.summary: India's Blue Tigers clinch their third consecutive SAFF Championship title by defeating Pakistan 2-1 in a thrilling final, showcasing their dominance in South Asian football.
articles.body: Under the floodlights of the National Stadium in Dhaka on November 17, 2026, India pulled off a stirring 2–1 comeback victory over arch-rivals Pakistan to win the 2026 SAFF Championship. The triumph secured a historic three-peat for the Blue Tigers and extended their unmatched regional dominance to a record 10th title.The build-up and high stakesThe summit clash carried immense historical weight. Pakistan arrived in their first-ever senior SAFF Championship final after eliminating hosts Bangladesh 1–0 in a tense semifinal, bolstered by five Europe-based reinforcements including captain Abdullah Iqbal and Easah Suliman. Meanwhile, Naushad Moosa’s youthful Indian squad, led by skipper Chinglensana Singh,had already edged Pakistan 3–2 in a thrilling Group B opener on November 5, setting the stage for a fiercely contested rematch.First Half: Pakistani pressure and stoppage-time breakthroughPakistan seized the initiative early, stretching India’s backline down the flanks with relentless pace. In the 17th minute, Muhammad Ali Khan nearly caught goalkeeper Arsh Anwer Shaikh off guard with an audacious lob toward an open net, only for a desperate deflection to send it behind. Early frustrations boiled over for the Blue Tigers as miscommunication led to two Indian players awkwardly colliding into each other in midfield, summing up a disjointed opening half-hour.India gradually found a foothold, coming agonizingly close in the 34th minute when Abhishek Suryavanshi unleashed a venomous half-volley that forced a sharp reflex save from Pakistan custodian Yousuf Ijaz Butt. Just as the half seemed destined to end goalless, Pakistan struck in stoppage time (45+1'). Junaid Ahmed Shah’s low pass deflected off Khaimingthang Lhungdim into the path of Alamgir Ali Khan Ghazi, who curled a clinical finish into the far corner to give Pakistan a 1–0 halftime lead.Second half: A red card sparks India's resurgenceStung by the deficit, India emerged transformed after the interval. In the 51st minute, P.V. Vishnu rattled the woodwork via a deflection off Butt as the Blue Tigers ramped up the tempo. The match turned on its head in the 59th minute when Junaid Shah was shown a straight red card for a dangerous stamp on Brison Fernandes.Reduced to ten men, Pakistan buckled almost instantly. Sixty seconds later (60'), Lhungdim whipped a dangerous cross from the right; Macarton Nickson’s initial effort was miscued, but the loose ball fell kindly for forward Suhail Ahmad Bhat, who lashed home a crisp first-time equalizer.Late heroics and historic gloryWith a numerical advantage, India laid siege to the Pakistani box. Moosa introduced fresh legs in Abdul Rabeeh and Irfan Yadwad in the 72nd minute, a tactical masterstroke that paid dividends in the 88th minute. Rabeeh swung in an inviting corner, and defender Sandip Mandi rose highest to power a bouncing header into the top-right corner, sparking wild celebrations in the Indian dugout.Pakistan threw everyone, including goalkeeper Butt, forward for a stoppage-time corner in the 93rd minute. India broke away on a rapid counter-attack with Lhungdim racing toward an unguarded net, only for Abdul Samad Shahzad to produce a heroic last-ditch recovery tackle. It proved too little, too late, as India held firm through five added minutes. Named Player of the Match, Sandip Mandi’s late winner, alongside post-match handshakes between both sets of players and staff, capped an unforgettable night of South Asian football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Madrid sigue bajo mínimos en la vuelta al trabajo
articles.standfirst: Sólo Mendy, Militao, Carreras, Courtois, Lunin y Rüdiger han estado a las órdenes de Mourinho a la espera del regreso de los internacionales
articles.summary: Sólo Mendy, Militao, Carreras, Courtois, Lunin y Rüdiger han estado a las órdenes de Mourinho a la espera del regreso de los internacionales
articles.body: El Real Madrid ha vuelto a los entrenamientos este martes para comenzar a preparar el regreso a la competición, el próximo sábado ante el Celta en el Bernabéu. Un regreso bajo mínimos, ya que la ausencia de los internacionales sigue marcando las jornadas de trabajo en Valdebebas. A la espera de que todos ellos se vayan incorporando, Mourinho ha dirigido la primera sesión de la semana con apenas seis jugadores de la primera plantilla: Rüdiger, Militao, Carreras, Mendy, Courtois y Lunin. Lo ha hecho reforzándose con la presencia de varios canteranos para completar el entrenamiento, algo que volverá a hacer en la sesión del miércoles. Rodrygo y Asencio siguen con los procesos de recuperación de sus respectivas lesiones de larga duración y Tchouaméni trabajó en el interior de las instalaciones. El francés, desconvocado por Francia la semana pasada por una lesión en el aductor derecho, es seria duda para el duelo ante el Celta. El Madrid no lo descarta, pero lo normal es que no se arriesgue y sea baja. Todo lo contrario que Bernardo Silva, con el que sí se cuenta para el sábado pese a abandonar tocado la selección portuguesa. La convocatoria internacional ha dejado numerosas ausencias en la Ciudad Real Madrid. Francia llamó a Mbappé, Camavinga, Tchouaméni y Konaté; Inglaterra a Bellingham y Trent; Brasil contó con Vinicius y Endrick. También se marcharon Valverde, con Uruguay; Bernardo Silva, con Portugal; Arda Güler, con Turquía; Dumfries, con Países Bajos; Brahim Díaz, con Marruecos; y Diomande, con Costa de Marfil. articles.title: Lookman, un mes fuera como mínimo
articles.standfirst: Las pruebas realizadas por el Atlético arrojan un esguince de alto grado, mayor del trasladado por la Federación de Nigeria. Se pierde, entre otros partidos, la visita al Barcelona
articles.summary: Las pruebas realizadas por el Atlético arrojan un esguince de alto grado, mayor del trasladado por la Federación de Nigeria. Se pierde, entre otros partidos, la visita al Barcelona
articles.body: Ademola Lookman estará lejos de los terrenos de juego como mínimo un mes. Lesionado con Nigeria el pasado viernes, el Atlético aguardaba su llegada a Madrid para confirmar que el esguince de rodilla leve que le había diagnosticado la Federación de su país no iba a más. Sin embargo, tras ser sometido a un estudio más exhaustivo por parte de los servicios médicos rojiblancos, las pruebas arrojan que su lesión va más allá, tal y como había adelantado MARCA. Concretamente, es de "alto grado", según confirmó el parte emitido por el club posteriormente. De ahí que, entre otras citas, se perderá la visita al Barcelona del próximo 2 de diciembre. Queda por tanto justificada la inquietud que reinaba en el seno del Atlético desde que el extremo se tuviera que retirar del partido que enfrentaba a su selección con Tanzania el pasado viernes como consecuencia de un golpe recibido en su rodilla izquierda. Había que confirmar que la distensión sufrida no derivara en algo más serio, por eso se trató de acelerar un regreso a España que no ha resultado sencillo por más que la Federación de Nigeria liberara a Ademola tras comprobar que ya no podría estar disponible para el siguiente compromiso. De ahí que, nada más aparecer por El Cerro pasadas las 13.00 horas de este martes, Lookman sería sometido a pruebas para conocer el alcance real de la lesión. Una vez examinado, el Atlético lamentaría que su problema es mayor del esperado, con un periodo de baja que, aunque queda ahora pendiente de su evolución, rondará el mes o el mes y medio. Obviamente no estará el domingo frente al Getafe ni el martes contra el Viking en la Champions, del mismo modo que tampoco lo hará en los siguientes duelos frente al Elche, el Barcelona, el Betis y el PSV. Una serie de partidos que puede ser aún mayor, pues su concurso frente al Valencia en el Metropolitano, justo el día que se cumple un mes de sufrir la lesión, también aparece en seria duda. De hecho, el debut en Copa del 15, 16 ó 17 de diciembre o la visita al Celta del 20 se antojan como un horizonte más alcanzable.

articles.body: Rodri encara la recta final de su recuperación después de la lesión que sufrió en el bíceps femoral de su pierna derecha en el encuentro de Champions disputado frente al Aston Villa. El futbolista no viajará a Azerbaiyán con el equipo para jugar frente al Sabah, pero la idea es que a su regreso ya se entrene con normalidad con el resto del equipo. Si no hay contratiempo, podría entrar en la lista del partido frente al Deportivo del domingo 29 para estar en buenas condiciones para enfrentarse al Atlético de Madrid el día 2. En un principio, se había hablado de un mes de baja para el futbolista azulgrana y eso significaba que habría llegado muy justo para el partido frente a los rojiblancos. Sin embargo, la recuperación ha ido mejor de lo previsto y podrá adelantar algunos días su regreso. En este momento, la probabilidad es que pueda jugar algunos minutos en Riazor. Rodri se ha convertido en un jugador fundamental para Hansi Flick. Lo había jugado prácticamente todo debido a su buen rendimiento. articles.title: Peter Storey: Former Arsenal and England midfielder dies aged 81
articles.summary: Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey - who helped the Gunners win the Double in 1970-71 - has died at the age of 81.
articles.body:
Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81.

Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals.

He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee.

"Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement.

"All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.

"We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund."

Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield.

He is currently eighth on Arsenal 's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions.

Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72.

He joined Second Division Fulham on a free transfer in March 1977 and made 19 appearances for the Cottagers before his contract was terminated later that year and he retired.

However, Storey had something of a troubled life after his retirement from professional football.

He was convicted of running a brothel - for which he received a suspended prison sentence in 1979 - and was later jailed for three years for his involvement in a counterfeiting operation, then served another prison sentence in 1990 for attempting to smuggle pornographic videos into Britain.

articles.title: 3.001 euros de multa al Real Madrid por una pancarta contra Tebas
articles.standfirst: Por "permitir" una con el mensaje "no es fútbol, son Tebas y Negreira" en contra del dirigente
articles.summary: Por "permitir" una con el mensaje "no es fútbol, son Tebas y Negreira" en contra del dirigente
articles.body: La Comisión Antiviolencia ha propuesto de sanción de 3.001 euros contra el Real Madrid por "permitir" una pancarta con el mensaje "no es fútbol, son Tebas y Negreira" en contra del presidente de LaLiga. La grada de aficionados del Real Madrid exhibió durante el partido contra el Sevilla, que se disputó el pasado domingo 18 de octubre en el Santiago Bernabéu, una pancarta en la que se podía leer el mensaje "No es fútbol, son Tebas y Negreira", con los nombres resaltados en colores azulgrana, además de corear cánticos en contra del presidente de la competición liguera. La iniciativa surgió tras la tensión institucional y la petición de dimisión del presidente de LaLiga por parte del club blanco. Por su parte, Tebas respondió acusando a la directiva del Real Madrid de orquestar la protesta. Por lo que ahora, Antiviolencia, en un informe, propone la multa de 3.001 euros al Real Madrid por "deficiencias en las medidas de control de acceso y permanencia de espectadores al no impedir la introducción y exhibición, hasta en tres ocasiones, de una pancarta de grandes dimensiones sin la necesaria comunicación previa y sin contar con el certificado de estar fabricada con materiales ingnífugos". Asimismo, el club Osasuna recibió una propuesta de sanción de 30.000 euros por "asctuaciones relacionadas con el apoyo a determinados grupos de seguidores, la autorización y utilización de elementos de animación y la gestión del Libro Registro de Seguidores, todas ellas infracciones de la normativa vigente en materia de prevención de la violencia en el deporte, tras analizar la actividad del colectivo de seguidores denominado Sadar Bizirik, así como su vinculación con el grupo Indar Gorri, a partir de los antecedentes existentes sobre la participación de integrantes de ambos colectivos en conductas contrarias a la legislación vigente". El Betis recibió dos sanciones: una de 30.000 euros y otra de 5.000 por "deficiencias" en las medidas de control de acceso y por la "activación" en la grada de numerosas bengalas y artefactos pirotécnicos durante el encuentro contra el Oporto el 14 de octubre y el Feyenoord el 21 del mismo mes en la segunda y tercera jornada de la Liga de Campeones, respectivamente. El Celta de Vigo ha sido multado con 5.000 euros por no cumplir la "prohibición" de venta y consumo de bebidas alcohólicas, al conocer que en los palcos VIP y en la grada de tribuna detectaron a varios espectadores con envases de cristal con marcas relacionadas con el alcohol durante el partido contra la Juventus de Turín el pasado 15 de octubre en la segunda jornada de la Liga Europa. Asimismo, 3.001 euros de sanción al Rayo Vallecano por "deficiencias" en las medidas de control de "acceso y permanencia" de espectadores al no impedir la introducción y exhibición de ocho pancartas sin "comunicación previa" durante el encuentro contra el Elche el pasado 24 de octubre. La Comisión Antiviolencia propuso una sanción de 60.001 euros y la prohibición a los recintos deportivos por un periodo de dos años a un aficionado que, teniendo prohibida la entrada, fue localizado en el estadio Municial A Malata de la ciudad de Ferrol, viendo el contra la Ponferradina, el pasado 31 de octubre de primera federación.

articles.title: Frenazo para el Cuti
articles.standfirst: El central rojiblanco sigue al margen del grupo y se perderá el partido contra el Getafe
articles.summary: El central rojiblanco sigue al margen del grupo y se perderá el partido contra el Getafe
articles.body: Pese a que el parón liguero se antojaba como la mejor ocasión para que el Cuti Romero se pusiera a punto y pudiera reaparecer este domingo frente al Getafe, lo cierto es que la recuperación del pilar de la defensa va más lenta de lo previsto inicialmente. En la vuelta al trabajo del Atlético de este martes tampoco se unió al grupo, con lo que su concurso en el Coliseum el próximo domingo se puede dar por descartado. De hecho, al Cuti sí se le vio este martes por el césped, pero para continuar su proceso de recuperación junto a los recuperadores. Así las cosas, teniendo en cuenta que su unión a la dinámica grupal aún se dilatará varios días más, su ausencia de cinco partidos desde que sintiera unas molestias en el RCD Stadium aún será mayor. Algo impensable cuando, tras perderse las citas frente al Sttutgart y el Deportivo, entraba en la lista para visitar al Levante. Sin embargo, una nueva lesión le obligó a volver a empezar. Este fue el motivo por el que el capitán de Argentina tampoco pudo estar disponible en los trascendentales duelos frente al Bayern Munich y el Barcelona, en los que su vacío se dejó notar especialmente. De ahí que ahora en el Atlético se manejen con pies de plomo para conseguir que su regreso a la competición se produzca con las máximas garantías posibles. Por eso no se está forzando su recuperación por más que lo ideal hubiera sido que ya estuviera en dinámica de grupo. De este modo, aunque el Cuti sigue dando pasos hacia su rehabilitación, no se marca ningún plazo para su reaparición, si bien se espera que a partir de la próxima semana ya pueda empezar a trabajar con el grupo, antesala de su regreso de una vez por todas a un centro de la defensa desde la que cambia por completo la imagen de todo el Atlético.
