articles.title: Dabo Swinney Defends His Record amid Clemson Hot Seat Speculation After Loss to GT
articles.summary: Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney defended himself and the football program on Tuesday as questions continue to mount regarding his future after the Tigers fell to 6-4 with Saturday's 20-6 loss against Georgia Tech.
articles.body:
Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney defended himself and the football program on Tuesday as questions continue to mount regarding his future after the Tigers fell to 6-4 with Saturday's 20-6 loss against Georgia Tech.

"All of y'all are quitting on the season," he told reporters . "Anyone wanna talk about Duke? ... I'm just trying to win this next game. We can sit and talk about all of this (big-picture) stuff after the season."

Clemson hasn't had a losing season since 2010, Swinney's second on the job at the school. His run has included two national championships, four appearances in the National Championship Game and 17 straight appearances in a bowl game or in the College Football Playoff.

But there have been concerns about his reluctance to embrace the transfer portal or adapt to the world of NIL as the college football landscape continues to change, and the Tigers haven't won a playoff game since 2019.

This year's team opened the season unranked, was immediately smashed by LSU in its opening game (51-10), was blown out by Miami (41-13) and has disappointing losses against Virginia Tech and Georgia Tech. Clemson is just 13-10 in the past two seasons.

Swinney, however, remains steadfast in his belief that Clemson will become a national powerhouse once more.

"We're gonna win a bunch more," he told reporters . "Coach Swinney's gonna win another national championship. I'm 56 years old. I've got a long way to go. A little rough patch right here, but I'll work through it. If you don't believe in me, that's fine. But I've got 18 years of reasons why to believe."

Nobody's doubting what Swinney accomplished in the past. But it's more than fair if Clemson fans are worried about what the present looks like and the future might hold with Swinney in charge.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel transfer news: Manchester United teenager announces departure from club amid Real Madrid agreement
articles.summary: Real Madrid reached an agreement with Manchester United earlier this month to sign JJ Gabriel; The teenager requested to leave United in September and has not trained with the club since; the 16-year-old and his camp are confident there is a clear pathway to the first team at Real Madrid
articles.body:
One source has told Sky Sports News a deal to take Gabriel to Real Madrid could be finalised in the next two to three days.

Gabriel is registered with Manchester United's academy until the end of the season but Real Madrid are intending to sign him in January.

There is a FIFA loophole that allows European clubs to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have a European passport which Gabriel qualifies for through both parents.

In a farewell post on Instagram he said: "Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020. as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams.

"Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

"You gave me moments I'll always treasure. To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

"As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ."

Gabriel did not make a competitive first-team appearance for United, but did make a senior appearance in United's pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan this summer.

The teenager requested to leave United in September and has not trained with the club since. When Gabriel's camp made it clear he wanted to move on, they asked to be de-registered immediately for the player to become a free agent.

Sky Sports News understands a big factor as to why Gabriel is leaning towards a move to Real Madrid is because he and his camp are confident there is a clear pathway to the first team at the Bernebeu.

Man Utd ready to move on from Gabriel saga despite losing teenage star

"Those on the outside of Carrington's walls will understandably view Gabriel's impending departure as a major blow for Manchester United. The reality, however, is that it has been expected for some time. "Gabriel and his family have no longstanding ties to United as a club. He was not born and raised in the north of England, where a sense of local connection might have carried greater weight in his decision to stay. "Over the last 12 months, United have pulled out all the stops to convince Gabriel and his family that there was a pathway to the first team. They met Sir Alex Ferguson, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick. Gabriel also trained with the senior squad and made his first-team debut at the age of 15 against Atletico Madrid in pre-season. "Ultimately, it was not enough to keep him at the club. As disappointing as it will be to lose a talent of Gabriel's calibre, United will no longer have to make further concessions to accommodate a young player and his family - a situation that can risk upsetting the balance of an entire academy system. "There is a wider consideration, too. Parents and agents connected to other academy players will inevitably take note when they see one individual receive such tailored treatment. It can create expectations that are difficult for a club to manage across its youth system. "This situation now appears to be reaching its conclusion. But the focus will soon shift to the 16-year-old himself. His talent is undeniable, but will the circus surrounding his exit become a hindrance to his development, or will it prove to be little more than a footnote in what could be a long and illustrious career? "Time will tell. And I imagine Jose Mourinho will have something to say about it, too."

'He could have been a superstar' - Merse on Man Utd losing Gabriel

"This kid's a good player. He could have been a superstar. Man Utd will be gutted.

"This rule has got to change. I think it's because his mum and dad have got an Irish passport that he's allowed to go abroad. And that needs to change.

"Manchester United have worked on this kid, made him the player he is. Obviously, he'd have been gifted at the same time.

"The thing is, he's going to Real Madrid. I said Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world. He's going to the biggest club in the world. It's not like there's not a player in the world who wouldn't go to Real Madrid.

"You ask any player who's playing in the Premier League, if Real Madrid come for you, it's very rare you turn them down. Great opportunity for the kid."

articles.title: JJ Gabriel se despide del Manchester United
articles.standfirst: La perla inglesa, de 16 años, publica un emotivo vídeo de despedida y su firma por el Real Madrid se realizará en los próximos días
articles.summary: La perla inglesa, de 16 años, publica un emotivo vídeo de despedida y su firma por el Real Madrid se realizará en los próximos días
articles.body: JJ Gabriel ya ha dicho adiós al Manchester United. La joven promesa inglesa, de 16 años, se ha despedido del club en el que se formó desde 2020 a través de un vídeo en sus redes sociales, con imágenes de sus mejores momentos vistiendo la camiseta de los Red Devils. El gesto confirma lo que MARCA venía informando estas semanas. Su salida de Carrington es ya un hecho y su firma por el Real Madrid está al caer. “Querido Manchester United, llegué en 2020 siendo un niño de diez años con grandes sueños. Aquí crecí como jugador y como persona, desde marcar en Old Trafford hasta recibir un premio al mejor joven del club”, escribió el futbolista. “Me diste momentos que siempre atesoraré; a cada entrenador, a cada miembro del staff, a mis compañeros y a todos los que me apoyaron, gracias por creer en mí y ayudarme a crecer”. El atacante cerró su mensaje mirando ya hacia el futuro, sin nombrar su próximo destino: “Al comenzar mi próximo capítulo, el Manchester United siempre será parte de mi historia. Gracias por todo. JJ”. Ayer, además, se oficializó su fichaje por la agencia de representación Epic, de Ali Barat, un movimiento que era un secreto a voces. Esas palabras de despedida llegan después de que Gabriel concediera en MARCA sus primeras declaraciones en España, en las que fijó su gran meta: “Mi sueño es ganar el Balón de Oro”. Su firma por el Real Madrid se producirá en los próximos días, tras tres semanas entrenándose en solitario en la capital junto a parte de su entorno. El United reclamará al club blanco en torno a 350.000 libras en concepto de derechos de formación. Una vez oficializado el fichaje, el atacante podrá ejercitarse en Valdebebas, aunque para competir deberá esperar a la ventana de enero, cuando se tramite su inscripción, y lo hará con el Castilla. En cualquier caso, el club de Old Trafford se resigna a su suerte. "No hay mucho que podamos decir. Aún no hemos tenido contactos con la familia, así que lo primero que hemos sabido ha sido a través de las redes sociales, como todos los demás", comentan fuentes del club inglés.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel: Man Utd teenager posts farewell message before Real Madrid move
articles.summary: TeenagerJJ Gabriel posts a farewell message saying Manchester United will always be part of his story, as he prepares for a likely move to Real Madrid.
articles.body:
JJ Gabriel has confirmed his exit from Manchester United with a farewell video message in which he says the club will "will always be part of my story".

The 16-year-old forward, who has a verbal agreement to join Spanish giants Real Madrid, walked out on United in September.

He has subsequently been training on his own in Spain after relocating with his family.

The 50-second video montage, posted on social media, begins with Gabriel penning a letter to United, and includes some of his notable achievements, including coming on for his first-team debut during a pre-season friendly with Atletico Madrid in Stockholm in August, when he was just 15.

Gabriel then thanks United's coaches and staff, plus his team-mates as he "begins my next chapter".

He has not returned to United since scoring a hat-trick in a Uefa Youth League game with Sabah in September.

Although United still hold the teenager's registration until the end of the season, it does not prevent him moving to a club in the European Union as he now has an EU passport through his mother, who is of Cypriot heritage.

Speaking to Spanish newspaper Marca earlier this month, he said his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or".

However, Gabriel has now broken his silence on his controversial decision to leave United, having won last season's Premier League Under-18 player of the year award, United's U18 player of the year award and been top scorer in a side that reached the FA Youth Cup final and Premier League U18 cup final.

"I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams. Here, I grew as a player and a person, from scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy [Under-18] award . You gave me moments I will always treasure.

"To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me; thank you for believing in me and helping me grow. As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be part of my story.

articles.title: Millwall open disciplinary proceedings against forward Benicio Baker
articles.summary: Millwall are undertaking disciplinary proceedings against forward Benicio Baker, BBC Sport understands.
articles.body:
Millwall are undertaking disciplinary proceedings against forward Benicio Baker following social media posts critical of senior figures at the club, BBC Sport understands.

The 22-year-old winger has played only for the Lions' under-21 side since joining from Brighton in February 2025 on a long-term deal.

BBC Sport understands the proceedings relate to a number of off-field matters, including social media activity.

Posts attributed to Baker's account, which has since been deactivated on Instagram but has been widely republished, appeared critical of senior figures at Millwall and suggested he "can't even train with the (under) 21s".

It is understood Baker was initially unavailable because of injury, but he is now the subject of disciplinary proceedings which, in the most serious circumstances, could lead to the cancellation of his contract.

Baker is also understood to be exploring options away from Millwall.

At the height of his career, Baker made six first-team appearances for Brighton under former manager Roberto de Zerbi, including in the Premier League.

The England Under-20 international also spent time in the academy systems at West Ham and Porto before making 14 senior appearances on loan as Port Vale finished second in League Two in 2024.

While at West Ham, before joining Porto, he was linked with moves to overseas clubs including Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Benfica.

Millwall have declined to comment, while representatives for Baker have been contacted.

articles.standfirst: La sub-21 termina 2026 con un empate (0-0) ante Albania en un amistoso donde chocó varias veces con el cerrojo local
articles.summary: La sub-21 termina 2026 con un empate (0-0) ante Albania en un amistoso donde chocó varias veces con el cerrojo local
articles.body: La Rojita despidió el año en Tirana, el escenario al que querrá regresar en julio de 2027, cuando el Arena Kombetare albergue la final del Europeo sub-21. La cita de este martes, sin embargo, no pasará a la historia por lo que ocurrió sobre el césped. Gran parte del encuentro discurrió con los de David Gordo empeñados en descifrar el cerrojo local, sin premio pese a su dominio y las ocasiones generadas en la segunda mitad. El seleccionador repartió galones entre los que habían mirado el amistoso ante Japón desde el banquillo. Solo Álex Valle, Marc Bernal, Peio Canales y Alarcón repitieron en el once. La primera, eso sí, fue de Albania. Un desajuste en la comunicación entre Jon Martín y Manu González lo olfateó Rashica, pero el meta bético, que se estrenaba con la Sub-21, resolvió con acierto. Pasada una fase algo diluida, Ángel Alarcón probó fortuna con un trallazo lejano que atajó el guardameta albanés. Poco más dio una primera parte en la que España fue tanteando, paciente, las juntas de un muro que no se abría. La reanudación no alteró el guion, y Gordo echó mano del banquillo. Primero fue turno para Mella, después para Iker Bravo y Pablo García de cara a revolucionar el ataque. Con el balón en su poder, España buscó a Espí por alto para inaugurar el marcador, pero los centrales albaneses apenas le concedieron un palmo. Tuvo una que acabó golpeando en Mella; de no ser por el fuera de juego, habría sido el primero. En el tramo final apareció Marc Bernal con la más clara hasta ese momento, un remate al larguero desde fuera del área dentro de una doble ocasión española. Enfrente, Albania se atrincheró prácticamente en su área, replegada como si defendiera la prórroga de una final. Volvió a insistir España desde lejos con un disparo de Ángel Ortiz que incomodó al portero local, y rozó el premio en el 87' con un cabezazo de Pablo García al que el meta albanés respondió con un estirón de reflejos sobresaliente. Aún lo intentó Iker Bravo con un remate en el descuento, pero el esfuerzo español se quedó en la orilla y el marcador tal y como se encontraba en el pitido inicial. Seleccionador: David Gordo. Árbitro: Genc Nusa. Amonestó con amarilla a Rodrigo Mendoza (51') e Iker Bravo (90'). Estadio: Arena Kombetare.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino Delivers Farewell Message to USMNT in Video Ahead of Manchester United Move
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino expressed gratitude for his tenure coaching the United States men's national team as he prepares to join Manchester United.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino expressed gratitude for his tenure coaching the United States men's national team as he prepares to join Manchester United.

"Thank you so much from the bottom of my heart for all the fans, for all the people that was supporting us in the last two years," Pochettino said in a video shared Tuesday by the USMNT. "Special, great memories of the World Cup and everything that we lived together. Always in my heart, always one of you. All the best and I wish everything good for the future."

Pochettino officially agreed to become Manchester United's next head coach on Friday.

His contract with the club lasts until the summer of 2029, according to David Ornstein and Adam Crafton of The Athletic.

Pochettino will continue coaching the USMNT during the squad's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match against Haiti on Tuesday before he's set to join Manchester United for a clash with Premier League rival Liverpool on Sunday.

The 54-year-old was hired as coach of the U.S. national team in Sept. 2024. The team posted a 22-12-2 record after Pochettino was brought in.

During the 2026 World Cup, the USMNT won two of its three group stage games before defeating Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 in the round of 32.

While the United States was ultimately eliminated from the tournament with a 4-1 loss to Belgium in the round of 16, the team was still able to earn its first knockout round victory since 2002.

Tuesday's matchup between the USMNT and Haiti begins at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Mou: "En 2013 me fui por amor al Real Madrid"
articles.standfirst: El técnico y Butragueño, en la inauguración del curso académico 2026/27 de la Escuela Universitaria Real Madrid Universidad Europea
articles.summary: El técnico y Butragueño, en la inauguración del curso académico 2026/27 de la Escuela Universitaria Real Madrid Universidad Europea
articles.body: José Mourinho y Emilio Butragueño fueron los encargados de inaugurar este martes en el auditorio de la Ciudad Real Madrid el curso académico 2026/27 de la Escuela Universitaria Real Madrid Universidad Europea. También asistieron al acto que da inicio a la vigésimo primera promoción Elena Gazapo, rectora de la Universidad Europea; y Marisa Sáenz, directora gerente de la Escuela Universitaria Real Madrid Universidad Europea, según informó el club. El técnico blanco tomó la palabra para compartir algunas experiencias con los alumnos. “El Real Madrid es grande por todo lo que ha ganado y también por sus principios y por su manera de estar en el deporte y en la sociedad. He estado fuera 13 años y en ese tiempo entendí mejor lo que la gente piensa del Real Madrid fuera de España. En 2013 me podía haber quedado, pero salí por amor al club y porque pensaba que en ese momento el equipo no necesitaba de mi perfil”. Mou dio las claves de su exitosa carrera como entrenador de élite. “Es una combinación de factores. Nací con algo y siempre me he preparado para el próximo paso. Las cosas parecía que iban encajando. Aunque tengamos a mucha gente alrededor, el entrenador siempre está solo y eso es duro. Hay que saber esconder nuestras debilidades”. Además, desveló una curiosa anécdota. “Mi padre estaba enamorado del Real Madrid y de Di Stéfano. Tuvo una carrera bonita como jugador y uno de los highlights de su carrera fue un amistoso en el Bernabéu, el partido homenaje a Gento. Para él y para su generación, Di Stéfano era el mejor de todos. Ese partido para los portugueses significó mucho porque nuestro héroe, Eusébio, nunca salió del fútbol portugués por razones políticas y en ese partido jugó con el Real Madrid”.

articles.title: Rangers great Ralph Brand dies aged 89
articles.summary: Rangers have paid tribute to Ralph Brand, one of the most prolific goalscorers in the club's history, who has died aged 89.
articles.body:
Rangers have paid tribute to Ralph Brand, one of the most prolific goalscorers in the club's history, who has died aged 89.

A Hall of Fame forward at Ibrox, the former Scotland striker, who scored eight times in eight caps, netted 222 goals in 347 appearances for the Govan side.

Brand made his Rangers debut as a 17-year-old in 1954 and remained with the club until 1965.

He was part of four league-winning sides and won three Scottish Cups and four Scottish League Cups during his time at Ibrox.

After spells in England with Manchester City and Sunderland, Brand returned to Scotland to finish his playing career with Raith Rovers and Hamilton Academical.

"Ralph Brand's contribution to Rangers was vast and, through his Hall of Fame recognition, he will forever be remembered as a great of the club," the Ibrox club said in a statement.

articles.title: Portugal se apunta a la 'lista Forbs'... y podría ser rival de España
articles.standfirst: Carlos Forbs, el 'heredero' del dorsal de Cristiano Ronaldo, hizo el tanto decisivo en la victoria lusa
articles.summary: Carlos Forbs, el 'heredero' del dorsal de Cristiano Ronaldo, hizo el tanto decisivo en la victoria lusa
articles.body: Se podría decir eso de que Portugal, sin Cristiano, no está muy católica. Pero también que a rey muerto, rey puesto. Carlos Forbs, que lució en este parón el '7' de Cristiano Ronaldo, conquistó en Cardiff la primera victoria de la 'era post CR7' para el combinado luso. Jorge Jesus respira y sella la primera plaza de grupo tras una noche muy complicada donde Gales, con total seguridad, mereció no perder. Un empate le servía a Portugal para, hiciera lo que hiciera Dinamarca en el Parken ante Noruega, asegurar la primera paza de grupo. Y aunque Gales llegaba sin opciones, ya muy lejos de su 'era dorada' comandada por Gareth Bale, expuso sobre el verde los colores y defectos de la selección de Jorge Jesus. Y eso que Portugal empezó ganando. Bruno Fernandes, a los once minutos, aprovechaba una recuperación alta de Joao Neves para, desde la frontal, marcar un golazo por toda la escuadra. Imparable para Ward. Empezó entonces el tiroteo. Gales reaccionó y dos minutos después empataba mediante Brooks. El partido se abría y Portugal empezó a sufrir ante una selección, la británica, en estado de frenesí. En el minuto 40, después de varias manos de mérito de Diogo Costa, Sorba Thomas no perdonó más. Una carrera larguísima, desde campo propio, y una definición perfecta ante el meta del Oporto. Qué partido estaba jugando el futbolista del Hull City. No obstante, ahora era Portugal la que reaccionaba con presteza. Esta vez fue Pedro Neto el que, también dos minutos después, hacía el 2-2 tras un centro de Trincao al segundo palo. El partido estaba 'disfrutón' y Gales se atrevía con todo. Al borde del descanso, Harry Wilson probaba suerte desde mediocampo y, también él, obligaba al portero luso a sacar una mano crucial que evitaba el 3-2. Fue la noche de Carlos Forbs. El extremo del Brujas, que luce ahora el '7' de Portugal, entró en el segundo tiempo y decidió el partido tras una gran acción individual. Fue el único gol en una segunda parte preciosa bajo la intensa lluvia que bañó Cardiff. Diogo Costa, de nuevo, fue héroe en los lusos y a Jorge Jesus le tocó sufrir en una recta final donde Portugal se quedó en inferioridad numérica tras ver Pedro Neto una doble amarilla. Pero los vigentes campeones de la Nations League resistieron y acudirán al sorteo de este viernes como cabezas de serie. Es decir, podrían ser rivales de España en cuartos de final. Gales, mientras, peleará por no descender a la Liga B.

articles.title: Wales 2-3 Portugal: Craig Bellamy's side lose final Nations League Group A4 match as Pedro Neto sent off
articles.summary: Match report as Wales lose final Nations League Group A4 game to 10-man Portugal in a 3-2 home defeat; Man Utd's Bruno Fernandes hit opener; Chelsea's Pedro Neto scored Portugal's second but was sent off in second half for two bookings in two minutes; Portugal finish top with Wales bottom
articles.body:
Although there was little riding on the contest, with Wales guaranteed a League A relegation/promotion play-off in March and Portugal having qualified for the quarter-finals, the two sides produced an entertaining spectacle.

Portugal skipper Bruno Fernandes blasted the opener after 11 minutes, but that was immediately wiped out by David Brooks' ninth goal for Wales.

Sorba Thomas broke free to put Wales ahead before the break, but again there was a quickfire response as Neto pounced to restore parity.

Substitute Carlos Forbs stroked Portugal ahead in the final quarter, and the visitors had to negotiate the final 16 minutes a player short after Neto was sent off after receiving two yellow cards in the space of two minutes.

Wales finish bottom of League A4 with one win and five defeats, and end a disappointing 2026 with a solitary victory, three draws and six losses from 10 games.

Portugal, meanwhile, finish the campaign as group winners as they earned their first win since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement .

Craig Bellamy's side had lost 1-0 in Lisbon in September in a game that was to prove Ronaldo's last for Portugal.

Ronaldo's subsequent retirement from international football probably had an impact on the attendance at Cardiff City Stadium, with some seats unfilled, despite the game being officially declared a sell-out.

There would be no clean sheet for Danny Ward on his 50th appearance as Joao Neves robbed Josh Sheehan and Fernandes lashed home from the edge of the box.

Wales responded immediately with Rubin Colwill twice involved, first setting up Harry Wilson for a shot Diogo Costa blocked with his legs and then Brooks, who swept home his ninth international goal, and second in two games.

Wales hit the front five minutes before the break after Brooks worked a one-two with Wilson before releasing Thomas, who advanced from his own half to slot past Costa.

The lead lasted three minutes as Neto lost Jay DaSilva from Trincao's cross to finish at the far post.

A breathless first half was not finished as Wilson hit the roof of the net from halfway with Costa retreating frantically, and the Leeds midfielder then forced a sprawling save from the Portugal goalkeeper.

Portugal regained the lead 20 minutes from time when Club Brugge winger Forbs - wearing Portugal's new-styled number seven shirt in the post-Ronaldo era - collected Ben Cabango's poor header and stepped inside Ben Davies to find the bottom corner.

Neto clattered into Brennan Johnson just one minute and 59 seconds after being booked, but Portugal held on for a fifth Nations League win to seal top spot.

Bellamy: That summed up the group for us

Wales head coach Craig Bellamy to BBC Sport:

"We knew in moments we were going to have to suffer due to the quality they have. The intensity wasn't there. We have a lot of players who don't play week in, week out a high-tempo game in such a short space of time. It's not ideal.

"We knew that at moments, when we win it, the spaces open. There were moments that worked really well. It summed up the group for us - really good moments for us; we make a mistake - at this level, these are normal things that happen.

"But also, that final moment. These teams have that profile to hurt you. At both ends, that last bit has caught us a bit in this group.

"Rubin Colwill is really good. There are times where he takes too many touches. You can't do that against this type of team. Five, six, seven - no! When he motors like he has, the ability to be a real top-end player. I'm very critical of him; I do love him.

"But I know there's more. That's why I wanted to play him in this A league. He's going to have to prove himself."

Wilson: We were better team in large spells

Wales forward Harry Wilson to BBC Sport:

"For large parts, we played really well again. At times in the first half, we had to suffer. They're a great team full of world-class stars. At times in our shape, we were comfy.

"But look at our three goals. We're disappointed. But for large parts we were really, really good again.

"We knew from the start it was going to be tough. The first game in the group against Portugal, we showed we belong. Against Norway, we beat them. In large spells tonight, we were the better team.

"Going forward or defending the goal a bit better, that's what we've got to focus on. We're going toe-to-toe with these teams; our shape is good off the ball."

articles.title: Republic of Ireland 3-0 Kosovo: Troy Parrot scores twice to send Heimir Hallgrimsson's side into the Nations League play-offs
articles.summary: The Republic of Ireland have finished as runners-up in Nations League Group B3; Troy Parrott scored two penalties to send them into the promotion play-offs; the win has also propelled the Euro 2028 co-hosts into a coveted pot-two seeding for next month's qualifying draw
articles.body:
The result ensured the Republic finished runners-up in group B3, and also propelled the Euro 2028 co-hosts into a coveted pot-two seeding for next month's qualifying draw for that competition.

Tuesday night's contest turned on its head in the 26th minute, when Kreshnik Hajrizi was sent off for handling the ball off the line, and Parrott took advantage with a top-corner finish.

The Real Betis striker doubled the Republic's lead from the spot five minutes after the restart, and Jack Moylan added a 75th-minute cushion to keep alive the hosts' hopes of booking a place in League A for the first time through the March play-off.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's lone change from Saturday's defeat to group winners Austria was the insertion of John Egan into the line-up, replacing injured captain Nathan Collins.

How Ireland finished as group runners-up...

It was a contest that lacked fluidity in the opening 10 minutes, before the Republic found a foothold and Finn Azaz looked to pick out Parrott, but was blocked.

Kosovo then twice missed chances to take the lead. Lindon Emerllahu fired just wide in the 17th minute, and Caoimhin Kelleher was called into action for the first time a minute later to deny Vedat Muriqi.

What had been a largely uneventful encounter suddenly took a dramatic twist in the 26th minute, a red-card incident sparked by Moylan's cross, glanced on by Liam Scales to Parrott.

His effort - clearly goalbound - was cleared off the line by Hajrizi, who extended his arm like a goalkeeper, and was immediately shown a red card by Latvian referee Edgars Malcevs.

Parrott stepped up and gave Arijanet Muric no chance when he rifled into the top right corner to set the Republic on their way.

It remained just a one-goal advantage at the break despite a handful of chances falling the Republic's way, while the visitors created one when Kelleher denied Ilir Krasniqi with 10 minutes remaining to ensure there would be no first-half equaliser.

There was a flurry of Republic chances immediately after the second half kicked off before Parrott added his second penalty.

Muric had just denied Jayson Molumby's effort from range and Parrott was rushing forward to meet the loose ball when he was taken down by the Kosovo keeper.

This time he dove in the right direction, but failed to stop Parrott from doubling the hosts' lead.

The Republic were less successful from open play, unable to put the game away from a string of subsequent chances despite finding themselves in plenty of space, and should have added a third before the hour.

Moylan's persistence finally paid off with 15 minutes remaining, nodding home substitute Liam Kitching's cross in off the post.

The Republic nearly added a late fourth when Adam Idah stung the palms of Muric with two minutes left.

articles.title: Hungary 1-1 Northern Ireland: Justin Devenny's superb strike fires Michael O'Neill's side into top tier of Nations League
articles.summary: Northern Ireland are in the Nations League top-flight after topping their group after a draw in Hungary; Barnabas Varga ended Northern Ireland's proud record of not having conceded in this campaign but Justin Devenny equalised
articles.body:
Barnabas Varga ended Northern Ireland's proud record of not having conceded in this campaign when he fired the hosts in front after 35 minutes - a goal that also sent Hungary to the top of the group.

But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for Michael O'Neill's young side, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland's one-point advantage as group leaders.

The visitors were on the back foot for much of the first half, with Hungary captain Dominik Szoboszlai hitting the post, but O'Neill, serving a touchline ban in the stands as former captain Steven Davis led things from the touchline, orchestrated key substitutions.

Northern Ireland started with Patrick Kelly in place of the suspended Jamie Donley up front but brought on Josh Magennis at half-time before Kieran Morrison and Brodie Spencer soon followed to help the visitors become a much greater threat going forward.

Magennis' physical presence and the extra pace paid dividends as, just two years after earning promotion from League C, Northern Ireland completed an unbeaten campaign in Group B2 to secure their place at the top table of European football.

How Northern Ireland earned promotion...

Without Donley, the lack of a clear outlet told in a first half that saw Hungary come forward time and again.

There was a big panic after five minutes following an uncharacteristic mistake from Pierce Charles, whose pass went straight to Bendeguez Bolla, a late change to the Hungary side, who whipped in a superb low cross from which skipper Szoboszlai struck the post.

Northern Ireland were pegged back but might have snatched the lead from a Ciaron Brown long throw in the 33rd minute. However, Tom Atcheson did not seem to realise how much space he had as he prodded a weak shot towards his Blackburn team-mate Balazs Toth.

Two minutes later Pierce Charles launched a long free-kick into the box. Brown went down under an Andras Schafer challenge, but as Northern Ireland appealed in vain for a penalty, Toth kicked it long. Trai Hume got his head to the ball but could not get it as far as Pierce Charles, allowing Varga to nip in and score.

O'Neill will have felt the frustration of his ban with his side trailing at half-time, but his changes worked regardless.

Terry Devlin, the matchwinner on Saturday, had already fired into the side-netting before Price's low strike from the edge of the box cannoned back off the post.

Four minutes later they were level. Hume's long throw almost fell for Shea Charles but instead sat up for Devenny to take a touch before thumping an unstoppable strike into the top corner.

As time ticked down, Hungary pushed forward in increasing desperation - with Rajmund Toth firing over late on - but Northern Ireland dug in with the defensive resilience which has been the cornerstone of this campaign.

articles.summary: Le remonta un 2-0 a Dinamarca con doblete de Haaland y un gol de Odegaard
articles.body: Noruega estará en el bombo de los cuartos de final de esta Nations League después de una remontada espectacular ante Dinamarca en Copenhague (2-3). Los noruegos iban perdiendo 2-0 en el primer cuarto de hora, con goles de Hojlund (11') y Hojbjerg (14'), pero los noruegos remontaron con tres goles. Empezó Erling Haaland, al que le habían anulado un primer gol por supuesta falta. Y puso el 2-1 tras un grave fallo del meta local, Hermansen, que intentó regatear sin éxito a Odegaard, que le robó la pelota. Fue el inicio de la tragedia danesa. En la segunda parte, Odegaard, en el 83', tras un remate dentro del área, y el propio Erling Haaland, tras un penalti marcado en el 96', pusieron el 2-3 que le da la clasificación a cuartos de final a Noruega y elimina a Dinamarca en un partido increíble. El penalti vino tras una clara mano en el área danesa en el minuto 93'. Erling Haaland transformó el gol en el 96' en su gol número 68 en 61 choques con Noruega.

articles.title: Brahim brilla en el triunfo de Marruecos con una bonita asistencia
articles.standfirst: Asistió de tacón para el gol de Ouazane en el 22'
articles.summary: Asistió de tacón para el gol de Ouazane en el 22'
articles.body: Brahim Díaz pudo destacar esta noche en el partido, válido para la clasificación a la próxima Copa África, que su Selección, Marruecos, ganó ante Níger (0-1). Marruecos, con los Bono, Bouaddi, Achraf y Zabiri (ariete del Racing), noqueó a Níger con un tanto de Ouazane tras mágica asistencia de Brahim. La jugada fue por la banda izquierda, aunque BD jugó por la derecha, y terminó en una internada del autor del gol tras una asistencia de tacón del madridista. Brahim lleva 15 goles y ocho asistencias en 35 partidos con Marruecos y acabó siendo sustituido en el minuto 84', siendo de lo mejor de su equipo. El partido se jugó en el Moulay Abdellah Sports Complex de Rabat, pese a que Marruecos era visitante, en teoría. Ante este mismo equipo, Níger, pero en el partido de ida jugado en esta misma 'ventana', Marruecos le metió 5-1 a Níger con una asistencia de Brahim incluida para redondear aquella ‘manita’. Achraf fue la sensación de aquel partido con dos goles y una asistencia. Recordemos que en esta fase de la Copa Africana de Naciones, con grupos de cuatro equipos, se clasifican para la siguiente fase los dos primeros de cada grupo. Teóricamente, aunque todo puede cambiar, sería una Copa África con sede en Kenia, Tanzania y Uganda y que se jugaría en junio de 2027.

articles.body:
William Blount football coach Robert Reeves has resigned from the program, he announced on Nov. 17.

Reeves wrote a brief social media statement indicating his decision to step down.

"To all my friends and family, ex-players and William Blount Community," Reeves wrote on X. "This was a hard day for me, but after much prayer and reflection I have decided to step down as Head Football Coach. I love all of you so much. God has blessed me. Go Govs!"

Reeves took over the William Blount football program in 2022 after former coach Philip Shadowens was hired at Knoxville Catholic.

Under Reeves, the Governors had two winning seasons and an overall record of 17-34. They reached the Class 5A TSSAA football playoffs in 2024.

William Blount went 1-9 in 2026. It ended the season with a 52-7 win over Campbell County.

articles.title: Mbappé, el goleador inevitable
articles.standfirst: Sus registros de peligro superan a los de cualquier otro jugador de LaLiga
articles.summary: Sus registros de peligro superan a los de cualquier otro jugador de LaLiga
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé es un goleador implacable. La actual temporada, casi inevitable. El 10 francés atraviesa un momento de voracidad extraordinario, hasta el punto de que sus estadísticas empiezan a dibujar un escenario poco habitual. Una amenaza constante para cualquier rival y una probabilidad de gol al alcance de muy pocos delanteros en Europa. Marca, genera ocasiones y concentra buena parte del potencial ofensivo del Madrid, pero lo más llamativo es la regularidad con la que sacude a todos. Los números respaldan su impacto: 17 goles en 16 partidos oficiales, una media de 1,06 por encuentro y tantos ante 12 rivales diferentes. Su producción representa el 38,64% de los 44 goles del equipo blanco. Pero hay un dato que explica todavía mejor su dimensión: según los registros monitorizados por Betfair, Mbappé tiene un 67,74% de probabilidades de marcar en cada partido. Traducido: de cada 3 partidos, Mbappé marcaría seguro en dos de ellos. Su superioridad también se aprecia al comparar sus opciones de marcar con las de sus compañeros. Si el 100% de las opciones de ver puerta se reparten entre todos los jugadores del equipo blanco, nadie tiene tantas opciones de ver puerta como él, como Mbappé. Acapara una media del 15,92%. Así expuesto, parece un número bajo, pero teniendo en cuenta que la media normalizada debería ser de un 5% aproximadamente (100% entre los 21 jugadores de campo de cada convocatoria) el resultado es que Mbappé triplica las opciones de ver puerta. Una barbaridad. El crack francés acumula 17 dianas ante 12 rivales frente a las 18 contra los mismos rivales (12) del curso pasado. El actual Mbappé está mejorando los números de pasadas temporadas. Suma 103 goles en 119 partidos totales. En ese histórico, su media es de 0,87 goles por encuentro. Ahora ha elevado su media de 0,75 inicial (primera temporada) a 0,95 (temporada pasada) y 1,06 en la actual. Además, en este curso, ha marcado en el 75% de sus partidos, incluyendo siete de manera consecutiva. Además, en expectativa de gol, no hay en Primera ningún jugador que sea capaz de generar tal volumen de acierto. El delantero francés tiene un xG de 13,98 goles esperados en todo el curso muy por delante de Raphinha, pichichi del campeonato, con un xG de 10,79 goles esperados en toda la temporada. Una prueba del potencial artillero de un Mbappé que, en la actual temporada, es cada vez más inevitable. Sin embargo, la única parcela en la que Mbappé sale perdiendo en la comparativa es la efectividad. Ahí Raphinha no tiene rival. El brasileño ha convertido en gol el 39,5% de sus disparos, prácticamente el doble que el francés (20,3%). También necesita muchos menos remates para marcar: 2,53 frente a los 4,92 de Mbappé. Una diferencia que explica por qué lidera la clasificación de goleadores pese a generar menos peligro. El madridista produce más ocasiones y acumula un xG superior, pero el azulgrana está siendo mucho más certero en la definición. El francés ha realizado 64 disparos, 34 de ellos a puerta, para firmar 13 goles en Liga; mientras que el brasileño ha necesitado 38 tiros, 19 entre los tres palos, para anotar 15 tantos. Lamine, el tercero en discordia, tiene una tasa de conversión del 15,6% (10 goles con 64 disparos). La amenaza también se traslada a Europa. En Champions suma cuatro goles, con 19 disparos y 13 remates a puerta. Sus 2,75 xG lo sitúan por detrás de varios de sus competidores en producción goleadora esperada, aunque mantiene su presencia entre los principales artilleros de la competición.

articles.title: Dabo Swinney Firing is 'On the Table,' Latest Rumors on Clemson HC Amid Hot Seat Speculation
articles.summary: Dabo Swinney has been a mainstay at Clemson for nearly two decades, but another rough season has his status as head coach in jeopardy.
articles.body:
Dabo Swinney has been a mainstay at Clemson for nearly two decades, but another rough season has his status as head coach in jeopardy.

Amid a 6-4 campaign for the Tigers, Swinney's firing is "on the table," according to Dan Wolken of Yahoo Sports.

"He seems to keep leaning on his resume, but I know people in the administration at Clemson are worried about what is going to happen if there's not a course correction," Wolken said on the Jim Rome Show . "I know that firing him is on the table, but it's also $57 million."
